title: Corporate tax cuts, merger activity, and shareholder wealth
primary_theories: agency theory of free cash flow

rival_explanations: some industry characteristic unrelated to DPAD (rather than the DPAD deductions themselves) drives the takeover activity
the CAR/synergy quality measures reflect investor perceptions and market sentiment bias rather than real deal quality
the DPAD cash flow leads to value-destroying (agency-driven) acquisitions rather than value-creating ones

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (publicly traded U.S. firms; DPAD-affected industries span Fama-French 12 industries, with domestic manufacturing/production most affected)
context.country_region: United States (U.S. incorporated public acquirers; sample includes both domestic and cross-border/foreign-target bids)
context.sample_size: 5072 M&A bids (main sample); firm-level activity tests use 106,506 firm-year observations

data_sources.name: Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP)
